title: Skill issue: Lessons from skilling up coding agents to use Langfuse - Marc Klingen, Clickhouse
talk_summary: Langfuse built a coding-agent skill to help users add tracing and evals, then iterated by inspecting traces, exposing docs/CLI search, and running basic evals. The main transferable lessons are to keep skills as thin references to live docs, instrument agent runs, and use fixture-based checks plus guarded auto-research to improve skills.

takeaways.technique: Skill with progressive disclosure and canonical references
takeaways.what_they_do: They package a skill.md with style guidance and module references, then point agents to live docs/CLI instead of embedding all documentation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: references for the different product modules to kind of like progressively disclose additional hints

takeaways.what_they_do: They instrument coding-agent runs and manually inspect traces to see where the agent wanders or uses wrong parameters, then update the skill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: looking at traces still like gets you to like 80% of the detail

takeaways.technique: Advertise CLI help and docs search
takeaways.what_they_do: They tell agents to use --help and expose a docs search endpoint returning relevant chunks/markdown, avoiding web/HTML fetching.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we just surface this uh rec stack again via like a search endpoint

takeaways.technique: Basic fixture plus LLM-judge checks on diffs
takeaways.what_they_do: They use sample repos and natural-language checks judged by an LLM on filesystem/diff state before and after running the skill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our checks are just natural language statements that we then via LLM as a judge try to um like evaluate

takeaways.what_they_do: They discuss timestamping skills and having the agent fetch or update if the skill is old, because embedded docs go stale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: So I think so just like time stamping it is enough. So when you use the skill, that agent can be like, 'Oh, this seems old.'

takeaways.technique: Auto-research skill improvements with target function and human review
takeaways.what_they_do: They define a target function and let agents propose skill improvements, then humans review and accept only sensible changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we accepted three out of the six improvements that were suggested
